tags: Pāṇini's affixes come with extra letters attached, like tags on a parcel. The affix शप् is pronounced just अ, yet it carries श् and प्. Tap each piece to find out whether it is a real sound or a tag.
detect: Which letters are tags? A handful of sūtras, 1.3.2 to 1.3.8, decide. Pick an item and I will show which rule marks each tag. ष्वुन् shows 1.3.6: an affix's initial ष् is a tag. And watch जस् closely: its final स् escapes.
flow: Now run the checks yourself, one rule at a time. Each question looks at the upadeśa as it is taught: a nasal vowel, a final consonant, the opening of a root, the opening of an affix. Some rules do not apply to this kind of item, some are blocked by a later rule. Then 1.3.9 deletes every tag at once.
strip: A tag has done its job once the item is named. Then sūtra 1.3.9 deletes it. Strip the tags from every item and see what is actually pronounced.
effects: So why carry tags at all? They switch rules on and off. The same root कृ gives कृत्वा, कर्तृ and कारक, depending on the tags of the affix. Compare the three.
flags: In programming terms, tags are feature flags stored inside the name. Toggle the flags on an affix and watch what would happen to the root.
quiz: Four questions, then a cheat sheet of the most useful tags.
